links.outcome: LLM error detection performance compared with human readers of varying expertise
links.effect: DeepSeek-R1 detection 83% vs junior radiologists 80% (P=.39) and senior radiologists 78% (P=.19); better than nonradiologists 66% and nonphysicians 38% (P<.001). Standalone LLM only; no human-with-AI arm.
links.quote: DeepSeek-R1 showed performance comparable to radiologists (83%, 95% CI 76%-89% vs 80%, 95% CI 72%-86% for junior radiologists and 78%, 95% CI 70%-85% for senior radiologists; P=.39 and P=.19, respectively) and significantly better performance than that of nonradiologists and nonphysicians (83%, 95% CI 76%-89% vs 66%, 95% CI 57%-74% and 38%, 95% CI 30%-47%; P<.001, respectively).

links.outcome: Comparison of eight LLMs and eight human readers on identical error-detection reports
links.effect: DeepSeek-R1 had the highest test-set detection rate at 89% (P=.001-.007 vs other 7 models) and matched radiologists (83% vs 80% and 78%).
links.quote: On the test set, DeepSeek-R1 achieved the highest overall detection rate at 89% (95% CI 87%-90%), significantly better than the other 7 models (P=.001-.007).

links.outcome: LLM error detection performance across Chinese and English reports
links.effect: DeepSeek-R1 and Claude-3.5-Sonnet detected 94% and 93% of errors in external English MIMIC-III reports; internal Chinese validation 83% and 80%.
links.quote: On the external validation set, DeepSeek-R1 and Claude-3.5-Sonnet achieved detection rates of 94% (95% CI 89%-97%) and 93% (95% CI 88%-97%), respectively.

unlisted_practices: LLM-based automated quality assurance of radiology reports (error detection and correction)
Prompt engineering to enhance LLM error detection

screen.reason: The study retrospectively evaluates and compares the accuracy of multiple LLMs and human readers in detecting and correcting errors in radiology reports using real-world retrospective data, without testing a specific organizational deployment practice.
